Hi Dev,

Thanks for the demo last week — Astra Labs is interested in moving from our current hosted tier into a setup that lets us add a couple of higher‑throughput features without a full Dedicated commitment yet. Two asks from my side: a) pricing for a conservative upgrade that lifts 2 feature modules (Reranker + Long‑context cache) into our existing plan with proration/credits, and b) clear rollback/rollback SLA language and steps (our procurement team is nervous about migration risk).

We value predictable spend and need a short pilot window to validate latency under load. Can you outline recommended migration patterns (feature‑by‑feature vs. full tier swap), what discounts we might get for committing 6 months, and what the rollback path looks like if we see regressions? Procurement is cc'd.

Thanks,

Hi Maria — great to hear. Quick summary below and attached a short workbook and migration map (migration-options-astralabs.xlsx, sample-migration-map.pdf) with cost sims.

Two recommended paths:

1) Conservative feature lift (recommended pilot)
- What: Keep current hosted tier; enable Reranker + Long‑context cache as add‑on modules.
- Billing: prorated monthly for add‑ons; we apply a one‑time migration credit to offset first month.
- Discounts: 10% off add‑on unit price for a 6‑month commit; additional 5% at 12 months.
- Rollback: instant feature toggle; prefix cache invalidation window (~2–10 minutes depending on workload).

2) Throughput‑first upgrade (Dedicated pilot)
- What: Reserved pool for predictable throughput, includes autoscale policy and burst credits.
- Billing: monthly reserved fee + per‑token consumption; we can structure a 3‑month pilot with reduced rate.
- Rollback: seamless failback to hosted variants via routing policy within 30–90s for most requests, longer for large KV caches.

Guardrails and operational controls we recommend for both:
- Canary rollout (5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%), automatic rollback on error/latency spikes.
- Preset downgrade window and credit application: if you opt to downgrade within 30 days we prorate and apply a migration credit.
- Ops playbook and runbook workshop (we'll run one with your SREs during pilot).

Next steps I suggest: 1) quick pricing quote from Lauren, 2) technical kickoff with Ben to map traffic/canary, 3) sign pilot amendment (link in HubSpot). Available for a call Tue/Wed.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Maria — looping in the pricing/contract details. See attached formal quote (quote-Astra-20270602.pdf). Highlights below: 

- Conservative feature lift (add‑ons only): estimated +$2,400/mo at your baseline request volume (this includes Reranker + Long‑context cache, computed from provided token profile).
- Pilot discount: 10% off add‑on unit rates for a 3‑month pilot; additional 5% for a 6‑month commit. Surcharges for burst gateway routing are waived for the pilot.
- Migration credit: one‑time credit equal to the first month of add‑on charges if pilot converts to a 6‑month commit within 60 days.
- Rollback SLA language (contract addition): "Redwood will provide instantaneous feature toggle-based rollback and shall initiate automated traffic reroute to the previous model variant within 90 seconds of rollback trigger; any data cache invalidation required will be completed within the standard maintenance window (maximum 10 minutes). Redwood will provide a remediation plan and credit if unmitigated errors exceed 0.5% of requests over a 30‑minute rolling window."

Procurement / legal asks we can support: redlined amendment to the Master Subscription Agreement, DocuSign-ready quote, and a short SOW for the migration workshop. I've added a DocuSign link and the HubSpot deal below.
